1276.r: Genitive with ὑπό, “by”: the agent [PREP:ὑπό]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

1277.r: Agrees with the subject of μετείχετε [TREE]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Passive: the subject is acted on [SMYTH:1735]. Circumstantial participle with μετείχετε [SMYTH:2054].

1284.r: ἀνάγκην ὑμῖν εἶναι “that you were under necessity”: the dative of the person with ἀνάγκη ἐστί [CONV:R2].

1285.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Articular infinitive [SMYTH:2025].

1286.r: τὰ ἐπιτήδεια … πορίζεσθαι “to provide your living”: πορίζομαι, the middle of providing for oneself [CONV:D3]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Dynamic infinitive completing εἶναι [SMYTH:1989].

1293.r: Future indicative of a coming event [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1294.r: ἐμοὶ μελήσει “I shall see to it”: the dative of the person with μέλει [CONV:R18].

1295.r: Future indicative of a coming event [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1298.r: Holden: “σὺν τοῖς θεοῖς, a standing (religious) phrase which corresponds to our D.V. = Deo volente” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:137] [PREP:σύν] [CONV:D1].

1300.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1302.r: ἔξεστι δ’ ὑμῖν “you may”: the dative with ἔξεστι [CONV:R18].

1311.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1314.r: τὸν αὐτὸν ἡμῖν κίνδυνον “the same danger as we”: αὐτός after the article means “the same” [SMYTH:1210].

1315.r: τὸν αὐτὸν ἡμῖν “the same as we”: the dative with ὁ αὐτός [CONV:R9].

1316.r: Accusative with εἰς, “into, to”: motion towards [PREP:εἰς]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

1334.r: Particular article: χρόνον is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

1338.r: τὸν μὲν οὖν πρόσθεν χρόνον “in former times”: the accusative of extent of time [SMYTH:1582].

1344.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1376.r: Holden: “ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ὁπλίσει … in hac autem armatura (quam videtis homotimorum)” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:138]: ἐν with the dative [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].

1377.r: οὐδὲν … προέξομεν “we shall in no way excel”: adverbial οὐδέν [SMYTH:1609].

1379.r: οὐδὲν ἡμεῖς ὑμῶν προέξομεν “we shall in no way excel you”: verbs of excelling take the genitive of comparison [SMYTH:1402].

1380.r: Future indicative of a coming event [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1390.r: Future indicative of a coming event [MORPH]. Future middle form with active meaning [SMYTH:806]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1400.r: ὃ πάντες εἰθίσμεθα φορεῖν “which we have all been used to carry”: the perfect passive with present meaning, “we are accustomed” [SMYTH:1946] [CONV:R6]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1401.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing εἰθίσμεθα [SMYTH:1989].

1408.r: The article makes δεξιᾷ a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1409.r: Dative with ἐν, “in, at”: place where [PREP:ἐν]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

1411.r: ᾗ δὴ παίειν τοὺς ἐναντίους “with which to strike the enemy”: the dative of the instrument [SMYTH:1507].

1413.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing δεήσει [SMYTH:1989].

1414.r: The article makes ἐναντίους a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1416.r: Future indicative of a coming event [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1417.r: οὐδὲν φυλαττομένους “in no way guarding against”: adverbial οὐδέν [SMYTH:1609].

1418.r: παίειν … οὐδὲν φυλαττομένους “to strike without any fear”: the participle agrees with the unexpressed subject of παίειν [SMYTH:2054]; φυλάττομαι, a direct reflexive middle [SMYTH:1717]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859].

1420.r: μή τι παίοντες ἐξαμάρτωμεν “lest we miss at all in striking”: the adverbial τι [SMYTH:1609].

1421.r: Agrees with the subject of ἐξαμάρτωμεν [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Circumstantial participle with ἐξαμάρτωμεν [SMYTH:2054].

1422.r: Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

1426.r: τί … ἕτερος ἑτέρου διαφέροι “in what could one differ from another”: an accusative of respect [SMYTH:1601].

1432.r: ἕτερος ἑτέρου διαφέροι “one excel another”: διαφέρω “surpass” takes the genitive [SMYTH:1402].

1433.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Potential optative with ἄν [SMYTH:1824].

1434.r: ἕτερος ἑτέρου … ἡμῶν “one of us than another”: the partitive genitive with ἕτερος [SMYTH:1306].

1436.r: πλὴν τόλμῃ “except in daring”: the dative of respect [SMYTH:1516].

1440.r: ὑμῖν προσήκει “it is fitting for you”: the dative with προσήκει [CONV:R18].

1442.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1444.r: ἢ ἡμῖν “than for us”: the dative with προσήκει [CONV:R18].

1448.r: νίκης … ἐπιθυμεῖν “to desire victory”: verbs of desire take the genitive [SMYTH:1349].

1451.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing προσήκει [SMYTH:1989].

1453.r: ἣ … κτᾶταί τε καὶ σῴζει “which wins and keeps”: the subject of the relative clause [SMYTH:938].

1454.r: The article makes καλὰ a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1455.n: TREE: τὰ καλά is the object of κτᾶται.
1455.r: Holden: “τὰ καλὰ πάντα, velut laudem virtutis aliaque eius praemia: τὰ ἀγαθά, ut praedam agros imperium (Fischer)” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:138]: the object of κτᾶται and σῴζει [SMYTH:1554].

1456.n: TREE: πάντα goes with τὰ καλά.
1456.r: τὰ καλὰ πάντα “all things beautiful”: πάντα agrees with τὰ καλά [SMYTH:1174].

1458.r: The article makes ἀγαθὰ a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1459.n: TREE: τἀγαθά is the object of κτᾶται.
1459.r: τἀγαθά “good things”: the object of κτᾶται and σῴζει [SMYTH:1554].

1463.r: Present of a general truth or standing custom [SMYTH:1877]; the plain present is kept first, with the customary present as the alternative [CONV:R12]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1469.r: ἢ ὑμῖν “than for you”: the dative with προσήκει [CONV:R18].

1470.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1478.r: The article makes πάντα a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1479.r: The article makes ἡττόνων a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1480.r: τὰ τῶν ἡττόνων “the possessions of the weaker”: the possessive genitive [SMYTH:1297].

1481.r: The article makes κρείττοσι a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1482.r: τοῖς κρείττοσι δωρεῖται “gives to the stronger”: the dative of the indirect object [SMYTH:1469].

1483.r: Present of a general truth or standing custom [SMYTH:1877]; the plain present is kept first, with the customary present as the alternative [CONV:R12]. δωρέομαι “present” is used only in the middle; the indirect reflexive type is the closest [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1485.r: τί εἰκὸς ἡμᾶς μᾶλλον … δεῖσθαι; “why should we need it more?”: τί “why” [CONV:R28].

1486.r: τί εἰκὸς (ἐστι) … δεῖσθαι “why is it likely that we need”: the predicate of an omitted ἐστί [CONV:R44].

1491.r: Accusative subject of the verb understood [SMYTH:1972].

1492.r: τούτου δεῖσθαι “to need it”: δέομαι takes the genitive of the thing needed [SMYTH:1397].

1493.r: δεῖσθαι “to need”: δέομαι, middle in form [CONV:D3]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Dynamic infinitive completing the verb understood [SMYTH:1989].

1499.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1511.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Imperative of command [SMYTH:1835].

Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Imperative of command [SMYTH:1835].

1516.r: Particular article: ταξίαρχον is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

1517.r: Holden: “ἀπογραφέσθω πρὸς τὸν ταξίαρχον … apud centurionem” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:139]: πρός with the accusative of the person one goes to [PREP:πρός] [CONV:D1].

1519.r: Particular article: τάξιν is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

1520.r: Agrees with τάξιν and takes its case function [TREE].

1521.r: Accusative with εἰς, “into, to”: motion towards [PREP:εἰς]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

1522.r: εἰς τὴν ὁμοίαν τάξιν ἡμῖν “into the same rank as we”: the dative with a word of likeness [CONV:R9].

1524.r: ὅτῳ δ’ ἀρκεῖ “whoever is content”: ἀρκέω takes the dative [SMYTH:1460].

1526.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1528.r: ἐν μισθοφόρου χώρᾳ “in the position of a mercenary”: the genitive of the person whose place it is [SMYTH:1297].

1529.r: Holden's index: “χώρα, locus quem quis in ordine aliquo tenet … ἐν μισθοφόρου χώρᾳ εἶναι” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:278]: ἐν with the dative [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].

1530.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἀρκεῖ [SMYTH:1989].

1532.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Imperative of command [SMYTH:1835].

1538.r: ὁ μέν “he”: the article used as a pronoun [SMYTH:1106].

1541.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

1547.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Circumstantial participle with ἐθελήσουσι [SMYTH:2054].

1552.r: The article makes ὅμοια a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

1553.r: Holden: “τὰ ὅμοια πονοῦντες, HA. § 716 b” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:139]: the internal accusative with πονέω [SMYTH:1573].

1566.r: Agrees with αἰῶνος and takes its case function [TREE].

1567.r: Particular article: αἰῶνος is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

1568.r: Holden's index: “διὰ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος, semper” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:239]: διά with the genitive of time throughout [PREP:διά] [CONV:R31].

1569.r: Agrees with the subject of βιοτεύειν [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Circumstantial participle with βιοτεύειν [SMYTH:2054].
